correctness.rationale: A fresh exact enumeration built the graph from the frozen LCF offsets (12 cubic vertices, 18 edges), computed all shortest distances by Floyd–Warshall, and for each of the 4096 subsets took its minimum separation count over all 66 unordered pairs. The full vertex set has minimum separation 6, so k=1 through 6 are the only feasible positive levels. Filtering by score and then by smallest cardinality yielded (2,4,5,7,9,11) with counts (2,73,7,35,39,6). Every one-out/one-in move between retained masks was tested and filtered by the Frucht edge condition for slides. Edge counts, component orders and all component radii/diameters matched the six certificate rows, with jump disconnection exactly at levels 3 and 4 and K6 at level 6. At level 6 the slide graph has components of order five and one. value.rationale: The Frucht graph is a standard asymmetric cubic benchmark. Minimum landmark count and fault tolerance do not reveal whether a deployed optimum can move to another optimum. The six-level example establishes concretely that feasible redundancy can increase while optimum jump connectivity disappears and then returns, and that even complete jump mobility can leave a slide-isolated state. Level-specific exact counts and distances are useful benchmark data for reconfiguration, not merely six isolated dimension values.
